# `activate_object`

Activate one or more ABAP objects. Supply either objectName+objectType for a single object, or the objects array for batch activation.

Defined in [`packages/adt-mcp/src/lib/tools/activate-object.ts`](https://github.com/abapify/adt-cli/blob/main/packages/adt-mcp/src/lib/tools/activate-object.ts).

## Input schema

| Parameter              | Type       | Required | Description                                                             |
| ---------------------- | ---------- | -------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `baseUrl`              | `string`   | no       | SAP system base URL (e.g. https://host:8000)                            |
| `client`               | `string`   | no       | SAP client number                                                       |
| `username`             | `string`   | no       | Username for basic auth                                                 |
| `password`             | `string`   | no       | Password for basic auth                                                 |
| `systemId`             | `string`   | no       | Logical system id (resolved via multi-system config or ~/.adt sessions) |
| `objectName`           | `string`   | no       | ABAP object name (single-object mode)                                   |
| `objectType`           | `string`   | no       | Object type (e.g. PROG, CLAS, INTF) (single-object mode)                |
| `objects`              | `object[]` | no       | Array of objects to activate (batch mode)                               |
| `objects[].objectName` | `string`   | yes      | ABAP object name                                                        |
| `objects[].objectType` | `string`   | yes      | Object type (e.g. PROG, CLAS, INTF)                                     |

## Output

The tool returns a single text content item whose body is a JSON-serialised object (`content[0].text`). On error, the response has `isError: true` and a human-readable message.

```json
{
  "content": [{ "type": "text", "text": "<JSON.stringify(result, null, 2)>" }]
}
```

See the source for the exact shape of `result`.

## Example invocation

```json
{
  "name": "activate_object",
  "arguments": {
    "baseUrl": "https://sap.example.com:44300",
    "username": "DEVELOPER",
    "password": "***",
    "client": "100"
  }
}
```

## Underlying contract

- `client.adt.activation.activate.post`
